1.explanation: AnchorsWithNoRelNoopener.afterPass is responsible for gathering all <a target="_blank"> elements missing rel="noopener". It currently does not filter out mailto: links, so mailto: anchors are reported and later modified. ExternalAnchorsUseRelNoopenerAudit.audit consumes those anchors and flags them as failures, leading to rel="noopener" being suggested (and applied) to mailto: links. To fix the bug, both the gatherer (to skip mailto: schemes in its selector or post-filter) or the audit (to exclude hrefs starting with "mailto:") must be updated so that mailto: links are ignored and not subject to the noopener rule.
1.bug_scenario: The “external-anchors-use-rel-noopener” audit is flagging and enforcing rel="noopener" on mailto: links opened in a new tab. When rel="noopener" is applied to mailto: links on Chrome for Android and iOS Safari, the link no longer launches the device’s mail client, resulting in a broken mailto: flow.

2.explanation: These two files form the core of the ‘noopener’ audit: the gatherer (AnchorsWithNoRelNoopener.afterPass) selects all <a target="_blank"> elements that lack rel~="noopener"—including mailto: links—and the audit (ExternalAnchorsUseRelNoopenerAudit.audit) further filters them by comparing the link’s URL host to the page host, but doesn’t special-case mailto: schemes. Because new URL('mailto:…') produces no web host, mailto links are treated as external and flagged. To fix, both the selector/filtering logic in the gatherer and/or audit should explicitly ignore hrefs that start with “mailto:”.
2.bug_scenario: The Lighthouse audit “external-anchors-use-rel-noopener” is incorrectly flagging mailto: links that open in a new tab with ‘rel="noopener"’. When the user adds rel="noopener" to a mailto: link, Chrome for Android and iOS Safari fail to launch the mail client and instead just open a blank page. The screenshots show the audit reporting mailto:sales@… and mailto:support@… as missing noopener, then on Chrome for Android the mailto:support@… link with noopener breaks.
